answer: RETIRED. Per-store mapping attrition -- the one gap backwards_window_store_density.json finding D4 left open -- is date-independent and negligible: 420 of the 421 stores that trade every backwards day already have a core.stores row today, against an independently projected h28 of 419. The method reproduces the landed control fortnight EXACTLY (571/571 stores, 485/485 full-window, zero set difference both directions), so this is a validated prediction, not an estimate.
consequence: No rescope. Queue s4,b1,b2,b3,b4,s5 stands; -b3 remains the critical path and its projected yield survives mapping attrition with ~1 store of loss. All three independent routes to criterion 3 (landed-streak donation 419, upstream density 421, mappability 420) now agree.

findings.finding: Attrition is date-independent. Backwards places map at 0.9715 (545/561), the landed control fortnight at 0.9711 (571/588) -- a differential of +0.04pp, with the backwards window marginally BETTER. There is no early-May cliff of departed stores.

The cohort that matters is almost untouched. Of the 421 stores trading every one of the 24 backwards days, 420 are mappable; exactly one is not. The control fortnight shows the identical shape: 485 of 486. Attrition costs the h28 projection ~1 store, not a tranche.

The method is exact where it can be checked. On the landed control fortnight it predicts 571 distinct stores and 485 trading all 14 days; core.transactions actually holds 571 and 485, with 0 predicted-but-absent and 0 landed-but-unpredicted. Every one of the 485 predicted full-window stores is a landed full-window store. So mappable => lands, with no observed slippage.

Independent reproduction of the density receipt. This probe recomputed the upstream side from scratch and returned 561 backwards places, 588 control places and 421 full-24 stores -- identical to backwards_window_store_density.json. The two receipts are consistent at the digest level, not merely at the headline.

Scope limit. This measures identity mappability, the only per-store attrition channel. It does not bound row-level quarantine from other reasons (INVALID_AMOUNT, STATUS_MAPPING_UNAPPROVED, contract violations), which reduce a store's ORDER count but not its presence on a store-day, and so cannot break a consecutive-day run. It remains no substitute for the post-activation verify.

method.control_range_rationale: Mapping attrition only threatens criterion 3 if it is DATE-DEPENDENT. Measuring a landed, attested fortnight identically turns an absolute count into a differential claim and cancels any constant bias already reflected in the landed measurements that produced the 419 projection.
method.database: oday_app on 127.0.0.1:6432 -- the instance the orders-history Job itself writes to (ODP_POSTGRES_DATABASE=oday_app, alfaloop-data-project:asia-east1:oday-plus-dev-postgres), NOT the PG16 activation target
method.landed_grain: scripts/models/sql/model_ready_views.sql transaction_daily: transaction_status='succeeded' AND currency='TWD', day = (event_time AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')::date
method.postgres_predicate: mirrors require_place: a core.stores row joined to core.brands on (brand_id, tenant_id) whose brand_code starts with 'fongniao_'
method.upstream_grain: distinct place per createdAt UTC day, state=TRADE_SUCCESS and currency=TWD
method.why_digest: The Atlas side runs in-cluster (private-pool IP allowlist) and the core.stores side runs locally over the Cloud SQL proxy. Rather than add a cloud-sql-proxy sidecar to a pod on a node already at ~96% memory -- which risks leaving it Pending and delaying the running slice -- the two sides exchange a fixed, documented, non-secret digest. No plaintext place identifier reaches the pod log, so the density probe's redaction discipline is preserved literally while still permitting an exact set intersection.

why_this_was_load_bearing: apps/data_platform/store.py::_PostgresLookup.require_place resolves every transaction's place against core.stores joined to core.brands, requiring brand_code to start with 'fongniao_'; a missing row raises MissingMappingError and the transaction is QUARANTINED, never projected. core.stores is a CURRENT-STATE dimension, so any store that traded in early May but has since left the upstream `places` collection would contribute zero landed store-days however densely it traded then. apps/data_platform/mapping.py::project_transaction needs no other identity lookup (no device, no machine, no member), so place mappability is the ONLY per-store attrition channel between a dense upstream day and a landed store-day.
